content: Ranitidine, when taken orally, is used to prevent heartburn associated with acid indigestion and sour stomach caused by certain foods and beverages. Studies conducted so far have not evaluated the safety of ranitidine for the treatment of uncomplicated duodenal ulcers for periods exceeding 8 weeks. Maintenance therapy for duodenal ulcer patients involves reduced dosages after the healing of acute ulcers. However, no placebo-controlled comparative studies have been conducted for durations longer than 1 year. Ranitidine is also used for the short-term treatment of active, benign gastric ulcers. Most patients experience healing within 6 weeks, and the benefit of extended treatment has not been demonstrated. Safety studies for the use of ranitidine in uncomplicated, benign gastric ulcers for periods longer than 6 weeks have not been conducted. Maintenance therapy for gastric ulcer patients involves reduced dosages after the healing of acute ulcers, with placebo-controlled studies conducted for up to 1 year. For the treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), symptomatic relief is typically achieved within 24 hours of initiating therapy with Zantac 150 mg taken twice daily. For endoscopically diagnosed erosive esophagitis, symptomatic relief of heartburn is commonly observed within 24 hours of starting therapy with Zantac 150 mg taken four times daily. Maintenance of healing for erosive esophagitis has been studied in placebo-controlled trials lasting up to 48 weeks. Patients with active duodenal ulcers, active benign gastric ulcers, hypersecretory conditions, GERD, or erosive esophagitis may use concomitant antacids as needed for pain relief. Ranitidine is also indicated for conditions such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, systemic mastocytosis, duodenitis, gastritis medicamentosa, hyperchlorhydria (including nocturnal hyperchlorhydria), and stress ulcer prophylaxis. Ranitidine should not be used by individuals allergic to ranitidine or other acid reducers. It should also be avoided in patients experiencing difficulty or pain swallowing food, vomiting blood, or passing bloody or black stools, as these may indicate a serious condition. It should not be used in combination with other acid reducers or in patients with kidney disease unless under the advice and supervision of a physician. Patients should consult a doctor before use if they experience frequent chest pain, frequent wheezing (especially with heartburn), unexplained weight loss, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain, or if they have had heartburn for more than 3 months, as these may be signs of a more serious condition. Heartburn accompanied by lightheadedness, sweating, dizziness, chest pain, or shoulder pain with shortness of breath, sweating, or pain radiating to the arms, neck, or shoulders should also prompt immediate medical consultation. If heartburn persists or worsens, or if the product is needed for more than 14 days, use should be discontinued, and a doctor should be consulted. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should seek medical advice before use. The product should be kept out of reach of children. There is no specific guidance from the Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) regarding the use of ranitidine in pregnant women. Ranitidine hydrochloride (HCl) is a white to pale yellow granular substance that is water-soluble, with a slightly bitter taste and a sulfur-like odor. Each Zantac 150 tablet contains 168 mg of ranitidine HCl, equivalent to 150 mg of ranitidine, along with inactive ingredients such as FD&C Yellow No. 6 Aluminum Lake, hypromellose, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, titanium dioxide, triacetin, and yellow iron oxide. Each Zantac 300 tablet contains 336 mg of ranitidine HCl, equivalent to 300 mg of ranitidine, with similar inactive ingredients. Ranitidine has an oral bioavailability of approximately 50% and a protein binding rate of 15%. The principal metabolite is N-oxide. The plasma half-life of ranitidine is approximately 2.5–3 hours in individuals with normal renal function, with the primary route of excretion being the urine. About 30% of the orally administered dose is excreted in the urine as unchanged drug within 24 hours. In elderly patients, the plasma half-life is prolonged to 3–4 hours due to reduced renal clearance. Pediatric studies (ages 1 month to 16 years) have shown no significant differences in pharmacokinetic parameters compared to healthy adults when adjusted for body weight. Ranitidine should be stored in conditions avoiding excessive heat or humidity. To relieve symptoms, one tablet should be swallowed with a glass of water. To prevent symptoms, one tablet should be taken with a glass of water 30 to 60 minutes before consuming food or beverages that cause heartburn. The product can be used up to twice daily, but no more than two tablets should be taken in 24 hours. The product is tamper-evident, and it should not be used if the carton or printed foil under the cap is open or torn.
